newsitem.title: USA: US Rep Archer seeks tax incentives for DC business.
newsitem.headline: US Rep Archer seeks tax incentives for DC business.

text.p: U.S. House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer on Monday called for a series of tax breaks aimed at spurring development in low-income areas of financially struggling Washington, DC.
Archer, a Republican from Texas, included the provisions for the capital in an $85 billion tax relief proposal he announced at a news conference.

Archer's plan would designate a series of low-income areas in the city as the DC Enterprise Zone. Businesses and individuals in those areas would be eligible for tax credits on wages and expanded tax-exempt financing.
The plan would provide a zero-percent capital gains rate on enterprise zone business properties that are held for at least five years.

Archer's plan would create an Economic Development Corp that could allocate $75 million in tax credits to developers and financial institutions that provide loans to DC businesses. The corporation also could issue tax-exempt bonds.
The residents of these low income areas would have their 15-percent federal income tax bracket reduced to 10 percent.
